title: Ranveer Singh Picked Up the Phone Himself. Now South Cinema's Quiet Star Is Walking Into a Zombie Apocalypse — and Bollywood.
excerpt: Kalyani Priyadarshan said no to a Hindi debut in a niche genre. Then the biggest star in the country called her personally. 'Pralay' rolls in August, and it's reimagining Mumbai as a ruin.
body:
She wasn't supposed to say yes. Kalyani Priyadarshan — the daughter of a legend, a Filmfare-winning natural, the woman who just carried a ₹300-crore Malayalam blockbuster on her own shoulders — had every reason to wait for a softer landing into Hindi cinema. A romance, maybe. A glossy multistarrer. Not a post-apocalyptic zombie thriller where half her screen time would be spent running through a digitally-rotted Mumbai. She was, by all reports, hesitant. So she said no.

And then Ranveer Singh called her himself.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=dKUeSoDGvAE

!Ranveer Singh — Photo: Wikimedia Commons

"The plan, as reported, is to fuse physical sets with cutting-edge AI-driven visuals to conjure a dystopia "unlike anything seen in Indian cinema." Bold words."

Not a casting director. Not an assistant with a calendar. The most bankable star in the country right now, fresh off the ₹1,200-crore tsunami that was Dhurandhar, picked up the phone and spent — by the accounts circulating in the trade — a considerable stretch of time walking her through the script, the world, the scale of what he was trying to build. He's producing this one too, under his shiny new banner Maa Kasam Films, his first time wearing the producer's hat. By the end of the call, she was in. That's the kind of pull a ₹1,200-crore year buys you.

The film is Pralay, and after months of will-they-won't-they rumours about creative differences and indefinite delays, it's now firmly back on the rails. According to the latest from Variety India, the project is very much alive and goes on floors in August 2026. The budget being whispered is a staggering ₹300 crore. The pitch: a large-scale, high-concept zombie thriller — survival, sacrifice, world-building — set in a Mumbai that's been digitally aged into a corpse of itself.

Jai Mehta will "reimagine Mumbai in The Hunger Games' style set-up," with large sections of the city "digitally aged to give it an abandoned look." — Mid-Day

!Mumbai — Photo: Wikimedia Commons

That directorial choice is its own headline. Jai Mehta — yes, of Scam 1992: The Harshad Mehta Story, one of the most beloved pieces of Indian streaming this decade, and the seabound thriller Lootere — is making his feature debut with a zombie epic. The team behind it is serious: True Story Films, Sameer Nair's Applause Entertainment, and Ranveer's own banner. The plan, as reported, is to fuse physical sets with cutting-edge AI-driven visuals to conjure a dystopia "unlike anything seen in Indian cinema." Bold words. Indian genre cinema has promised that before and blinked. This one has the money and the muscle to actually try.

Which brings us back to Kalyani — because casting her is the most interesting decision in the whole package. For the unfamiliar diaspora viewer, here's who's arriving: the daughter of director Priyadarshan, the comedy maestro behind Hera Pheri and Hungama, who began her own career not in front of the camera but behind it, as an assistant art director. She made her acting debut with the Telugu film Hello! in 2017 and promptly won the Filmfare Award for Best Female Debut – South. Then came Varane Avashyamund, Maanaadu, the aching Hridayam — performances built on stillness and a kind of understated screen presence that doesn't shout for attention but holds it anyway. And most recently, Lokah Chapter 1: Chandra, the Malayalam superhero film that became a genuine nationwide phenomenon and turned her from respected South star into pan-India name.

She is, in other words, exactly the kind of actor Bollywood keeps importing from the South these days — and exactly the kind who tends to walk in and quietly out-act everyone in the frame. Her character in Pralay reportedly demands a blend of emotional depth and full-throttle action, and she's already begun prep. The pairing — Ranveer's maximalist, vein-popping intensity against her watchful calm — could be electric, or it could be a fascinating mismatch. Either way it's worth the ticket.

There's a larger story humming underneath all this. Pralay is part of a visible shift in how India's biggest stars are working — blocking out vast windows for single, swing-for-the-fences projects rather than juggling five films at once. Ranveer himself walked away from Don 3 to clear the runway. The industry, flush from a run of mythological and high-concept epics, is betting big on world-building and global appeal. A zombie apocalypse set in a recognisable Indian metropolis, in Hindi, with a South superstar as its emotional anchor — that's a film designed to travel.

For NRI audiences in the US, UK and Canada, Pralay is a 2027 theatrical release on the horizon — expect a wide overseas rollout given Ranveer's post-Dhurandhar draw, likely with Tamil and Telugu dubs to capture Kalyani's existing Southern base, and an eventual streaming home to be announced. Shooting starts in Mumbai this August, with the production moving to other locations after the city sequences wrap.

It began with a phone call she almost didn't take. If Pralay lands the way its makers are betting, that call may turn out to be one of the smartest things Ranveer Singh did all year.
